title: Proposal to extend retirement age of SC and AC judges will create unrest in state sector
byline: The Government’s proposal to extend the retirement age of only Supreme Court (SC) and Appeal Court (AC) judges will create unrest in the legal fraternity and the state sector as a whole, the Opposition alleged yesterday.

title: Met. predicts rain
byline: Amid the prevailing hot weather, the Department of Meteorology has predicted the return of rains, with atmospheric conditions becoming favourable for afternoon thundershowers in most parts of the island.

title: Doctors urge parents to bathe children twice daily
byline: Amid predicted water cuts, medical experts have urged parents to ensure their children bathe at least twice a day to prevent dehydration and heat-related illnesses due to rising temperatures across the country.

title: Trump levels new threats against Iran, says bridges ‘next’
byline: Trump has levelled a series of new threats against Iran, warning that the US military “hasn’t even started” destroying what remains of Iranian infrastructure.

title: Are we running out of drinking water?
byline: Major reservoirs supplying fresh water to thousands of households in the main Colombo District is soon drying up posing a threat of drinking water becoming scarce in the coming weeks.

title: US Army chief of staff fired by Hegseth, sources say
byline: U.S. Army Chief ​of Staff Randy George was fired on Thursday by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, three U.S. defense officials told Reuters, in ‌the latest purge among the Pentagon’s most senior ranks.

title: NDB probes Rs. 380 mn internal fraud
byline: National Development Bank PLC (NDB) said it has launched a probe into an internal fraud involving employees and third parties, with early estimates pointing to a potential loss of about 380 million Sri Lankan rupees, that could rise.

title: Canadian national nabbed with over 21kg of Kush at BIA
byline: A 42-year-old Canadian national was arrested by the Police Narcotic Bureau (PNB) at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) early this morning. The arrest took place at the arrival terminal following a specialized operation conducted by the airport unit of the PNB.

title: ’Be serious... don’t speak every day’: Macron criticises Trump approach to Iran war
byline: The Iran war requires a ’’serious’’ approach that does not change every day, Emmanuel Macron has said, in an apparent reference to US President Donald Trump’s seemingly contradictory remarks about the conflict.

title: Moscow to compensate families of Sri Lankan forces killed in Russia
byline: Russian Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Andrey Rudenko has agreed to initiate the necessary procedures to provide compensation for the families of Sri Lankan security forces personnel who lost their lives while in Russia.

title: Trump removes US Attorney General Pam Bondi
byline: US President Donald Trump has removed Attorney General Pam Bondi - a longtime ally and fierce defender of his administration - from her post as America’s top law enforcement officer.

title: CSE Starts April Mixed as Early Gains Fade Amid Cautious Sentiment
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange commenced the month of April on a mixed note on 01st April 2026, with the ASPI closing in positive territory while the S&P SL20 ended marginally lower. The market showed early strength, with the ASPI gaining over 140 points at its peak during the session; however, these gains were not sustained as selling pressure emerged, leading to a gradual pullback.

title: Nuwan Thushara takes Sri Lanka Cricket to Court
byline: Sri Lanka cricketer Nuwan Thushara has filed a plaint before the Colombo District Court challenging the refusal of Sri Lanka Cricket to provide him with what is known as a No Objection Certificate (NOC) to ensure he could play for his franchise team at the sport’s most lucrative showpiece called the Indian Premier League (IPL) which commenced last week.

title: Russia bans producers from exporting gasoline until end-July
byline: Russia has imposed a ban on ​gasoline exports for producers of the ‌fuel until the end of July, the government said on Thursday.

title: IMF delegation meets Speaker, MPs ahead of key review
byline: A delegation from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) met with the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, and Party Leaders of the Sri Lankan Parliament in preparation for the upcoming Fifth and Sixth Review Mission scheduled from 26 March to 8 April 2026.

title: FIFA raises top ticket price for World Cup final to $10,990
byline: The first open sale of tickets for the 2026 World Cup showed Fifa is charging up to $10,990 (£8,333) to be at the final.

title: Decades-old murder cases end with death sentences
byline: The Nuwara Eliya High Court sentenced four individuals to death in three long-running murder cases.

title: Four children killed in nursery school stabbing attack in Uganda
byline: A man has killed four children in a stabbing attack at a nursery school in the Ugandan capital, Kampala, police have said.

title: Nighttime water cuts to affect key Colombo suburbs until April 10
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) said that three-hour water cuts will be imposed in Battaramulla, Pamankada, Wellawatte, Nawala and surrounding areas on every other day from today (April 2) until April 10 from 10.00 p.m. to 1.00 a.m.

title: Sri Lanka Cricket appoints two new national coaches
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has appointed Ryan van Niekerk as the National Bowling Coach and Jordan Gregory as the National Fielding and Spin Bowling Coach.

title: Online systems to expand across public service by April 20
byline: The third meeting of the Cabinet-appointed committee tasked with ensuring the continuous functioning of the public service, was held under the patronage of Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya, via virtual platform.

title: TPA mets President to discuss Malayagam Community issues
byline: A group of Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA) members, led by Mano Ganesan, met President Anura Kumara Dissanayake this morning (02) at the Presidential Secretariat.

title: Court grants bail to insurance company Engineer in alleged bribery case
byline: The Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court ordered the release on bail of an engineer attached to Continental Lanka Insurance Company, who had been remanded over allegations of aiding and abetting the offering of a bribe to an Additional Government Analyst of the Government Analyst’s Department.

title: New Chief of Staff appointed to Sri Lanka Army
byline: Major General Manada Yahampath of the Sri Lanka Light Infantry has been appointed as the 68th Chief of Staff of the Sri Lanka Army, effective today (02 April 2026).

title: Govt moves to regulate elder care institutions with new guidelines
byline: The government is taking steps to introduce regulations and guidelines to standardize institutions providing residential care for senior citizens, in line with broader efforts to safeguard their rights and well-being.

title: Namal accuses President of shielding ‘Coal Scam’ suspects
byline: The Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer Namal Rajapaksa today alleged that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is complicit in an alleged coal-related fraud, claiming the government is protecting those involved.

title: Zero tolerance for corporal punishment in schools reiterated
byline: The Education Ministry has reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining discipline in schools while strictly prohibiting any form of corporal punishment or psychological harm to students.

title: Water supply to be managed until April 20 as river levels drop
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board warned that water supply across the island will be managed until April 20 due to the rapidly declining river levels caused by prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Iran ‘will not tolerate vicious cycle of war, negotiations, ceasefire’
byline: Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman has issued a statement in response to Trump’s speech, in which the US president warned that Iran must agree to a deal within two to three weeks or face strikes on every one of its power plants.

title: Severe lightning alerts issued for several provinces
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued an advisory for severe lightning affecting several parts of the country, including the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, North Western and Uva provinces, as well as the Galle, Matara and Anuradhapura districts.

title: Myanmar’s coup leader elected president by pro-military parliament
byline: Myanmar’s coup leader has won a parliamentary vote to become the ⁠country’s president, formalising his grip on political power in the war-torn nation five years after he ousted an elected government.

title: US-based monks to lead Peace Walk in Sri Lanka
byline: A discussion on providing state patronage for the upcoming “Walk for Peace Programme in Sri Lanka” was held at the Presidential Secretariat, with the participation of a group of Venerable monks who recently completed a 110-day peace walk across 10 states in the United States, from Texas to Washington.

title: Kuwait oil refinery damaged in drone attack
byline: Kuwait’s state news agency said on X that an oil refinery in Al Ahmadi, operated by the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation, was attacked in an early morning drone strike on Friday.

title: Police arrest 147 foreign nationals in Chilaw hotel raid
byline: Police arrested 147 foreign nationals during a raid conducted at a hotel in Iranavila, Chilaw, police said.

title: Heavy rains in Nuwara Eliya
byline: Heavy thunder showers were experienced in several areas in the Nuwara Eliya district last evening, much to the relief of the people who had been affected by the prolonged dry weather and intense heat.

title: Rains predicted in most parts of island
byline: Amid the prevailing hot weather, the Department of Meteorology has predicted the return of rains, with atmospheric conditions becoming favourable for afternoon thundershowers in most parts of the island.

title: Trump levels new threats against Iran, says bridges ‘next’
byline: Trump has levelled a series of new threats against Iran, warning that the US military “hasn’t even started” destroying what remains of Iranian infrastructure.

title: Pakistan hikes fuel prices sharply amid spiralling Mideast conflict
byline: Pakistan on Thursday hiked consumer ​prices for diesel and petrol sharply, its second increase in less than ‌a month, amid rising global oil prices spurred by the conflict in the Middle East.

title: Cuba to free 2,010 prisoners from island jails in ’sovereign gesture’
byline: Cuba on Thursday said ​it would free more than 2,000 prisoners from the ‌island’s jails, according to state-run media, the second time this year its communist-run government has announced a prisoner amnesty amid talks with the administration of ​U.S. president Donald Trump.

title: Brent crude hovers around $109 a barrel as war continues
byline: Oil prices have surged following Trump’s renewed threats to destroy Iranian infrastructure.

title: Myanmar’s coup leader elected president by pro-military parliament
byline: Myanmar’s coup leader has won a parliamentary vote to become the ⁠country’s president, formalising his grip on political power in the war-torn nation five years after he ousted an elected government.

title: Pakistan hikes fuel prices sharply amid spiralling Mideast conflict
byline: Pakistan on Thursday hiked consumer ​prices for diesel and petrol sharply, its second increase in less than ‌a month, amid rising global oil prices spurred by the conflict in the Middle East.

title: Royal-Trinity Blockbuster at the Stadium
byline: The curtains of the Dialog Schools Rugby Knockout tournament will come down tomorrow (04) with Trinity, the league champions and knockout runners-up of 2025, clashing against arch Bradby Shield rivals Royal in quest for the title to be kicked off tomorrow at the Sugathadasa Stadium from 4.15 p.m. onwards.

title: Iran shoots down U.S. F-15 fighter in humiliation for Trump
byline: Iran claims it has shot down an American fighter jet over the country for the first time, according to its own media and a source who confirmed it to a well-connected Israeli American journalist.

title: Israel’s PM says 70% of Iran’s steel production capacity destroyed, hindering weapons production
byline: Friday began with Israel saying it was under attack by a new barrage of missiles from Iran, as President Donald Trump warned the United States had yet to begin ’’destroying what’s left’’ of the Islamic republic’s infrastructure.

title: Four inmates escape Kandakadu Rehabilitation Centre
byline: Four inmates have reportedly escaped from the Kandakadu Treatment and Rehabilitation Centre in Polonnaruwa this afternoon (03).

title: Doctors to continue ongoing strike, challenge Health Minister
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) announced that its strike action will continue from 8.00 a.m. tomorrow (04), citing unresolved concerns over what it describes as unfair transfers.

title: Water cut duration reduced to 18 hours
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board has announced that the ongoing 24-hour water cut imposed in several areas will be reduced to 18 hours.

title: NASA releases stunning first images of Earth taken by the Artemis II astronauts
byline: NASA released the very first images taken by astronauts aboard the Artemis II Orion capsule as they are making their way to the moon.

title: Over dozen Generals removed since Hegseth took office
byline: The United States military is undergoing a sweeping leadership shake-up, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth overseeing the removal of more than a dozen senior generals and admirals since early 2025.

title: Saunders and St. Mary’s set for final showdown tomorrow
byline: Two of Sri Lanka’s historic football clubs, Saunders SC Colombo and St. Mary’s SC Jaffna, will clash in the final of the FFSL Champions Cup 2025–26 knockout tournament tomorrow (April 4) at 6.00 p.m. at the Racecourse Grounds in Colombo.
